mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher when FEDFUNDS is low.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns remain positive despite unemployment increase.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment combined with employment growth indicates a strong economy, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are negative with low unemployment and employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate in late-cycle indicates tightening, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are positive when FEDFUNDS is high in late-cycle.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts reflect strong demand, positively influencing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are negative with rising housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production indicates economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are positive when industrial production is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales and low interest rates indicate strong demand and easy money, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are negative with rising retail sales and low rates.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment in early-cycle expansion signals recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns are negative with low unemployment in early-cycle.
